newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH COOPERATIVE BANKS VOW TO INCREASE OFFER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH COOPERATIVE BANKS VOW TO INCREASE OFFER.

text.p: Polish cooperative bank officials vowed to widen the scope of services their banks offer at a meeting commemorating 135 years of cooperative banking in Poland, PAP news agency said on Sunday.

PAP said co-operative bank officials announced that their banks would increase their activities to include trading of treasuries, selling insurance policies, creating new forms of credit and a larger range of non-cash transactions.

Some 1,270 of the country's 1,500 cooperative banks are grouped under Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ), undergoing a restructuring process to solve problems arising from its huge bad debt portfolio, which ammounted to 2.5 billion zlotys at the end of 1994.
BGZ turned a 391 million zloty net profit in 1995 after years of being in the red. It had said its profit would increase further this year.
